questions.prompt: The Nara and Kunama belong to the ___ language group.
questions.explanation:
Textbook: Nilotic – Nara and Kunama; Cushitic – Hidareb, Bilen, Saho, Afar; Semitic – Tigrinya, Tigre, Rashaida.
Answer: Nilotic.

questions.prompt: The two Bilen groups around Keren were organised on the basis of:
questions.explanation:
Textbook: 'Both Bilen groups were organized on the basis of kinship.'
Answer: kinship.

questions.prompt: Which group suffered most from the raids of the Tigrean feudal lords, losing about two-thirds of its people?
questions.explanation:
Textbook: 'Especially hard hit were the Nara and Kunama… two-thirds of them were killed.'
Answer: The Nara and Kunama.

questions.prompt: The period of Abyssinian history when regional lords became powerful and independent (second half of the 18th century) is called:
questions.explanation:
The decline of central power gave rise to the 'Era of Princes' or Zemene Mesafint.
Answer: Zemene Mesafint (Era of Princes).

questions.prompt: The Beja created how many independent kingdoms in Eritrea?
questions.explanation:
Textbook: Naqis, Baqlin, Bazin, Jarin and Qat'a – five kingdoms.
Answer: Five.

questions.prompt: A one-million-year-old hominid cranium was discovered in Eritrea at
questions.explanation:
Textbook: 'one million year old hominid cranium in Buya, northern Danakil Depression'.
Answer: Buya.

questions.prompt: Islam spread into Eritrea mainly through
questions.explanation:
Textbook: trade routes were the major channels of penetration of Islam.
Answer: trade and trade routes.

questions.prompt: The Beja kingdom of Baqlin depended mainly on
questions.explanation:
Textbook: 'Baqlin depended on camel and cattle herding.'
Answer: camel and cattle herding.

questions.prompt: Egyptian forces were defeated by Yohannes IV in 1875–76 at
questions.explanation:
Egyptian defeats: Gundet (1875) and Gura (1876).
Answer: Gundet and Gura.

questions.prompt: Between which centuries did the Beja dominate much of Eritrea?
questions.explanation:
Textbook: Beja expansion and rule between the 8th and 14th centuries.
Answer: 8th–14th.

questions.prompt: The discovery at Buya shows that Eritrea was
options: the centre of the Aksumite kingdom
part of the region where the first humans lived
questions.explanation:
Textbook 6.1: Buya testifies that Eritrea was inhabited by the first humans (the Great Rift Valley region).
Answer: part of the region where the first humans lived.

questions.prompt: The Dahlak Sultanate was among the first centres of
options: Islam in the Horn of Africa
questions.explanation:
Textbook: 'Among the first Islamic centers was the sultanate of Dahlak, established in the 8th century.'
Answer: Islam in the Horn of Africa.

questions.prompt: Bahri Negassi was the title of the rulers of
questions.explanation:
Textbook: 'Bahri Negassi was a title used by the rulers of Medri Bahri, a territory which covered the highlands of Eritrea.'
Answer: Medri Bahri.

questions.prompt: Which of the following Eritrean ethnic groups belongs to the Nilotic language family?
questions.explanation:
Textbook: 'Nilotic language group: Nara and Kunama.'
Answer: Kunama.

questions.prompt: After the battle of Gundet, Emperor Yohannes IV recognised Woldemichael Solomon as ruler of
questions.explanation:
Textbook: 'Emperor Yohannes IV recognized him as ruler of Hamasien. He also was given the title Degiat.'
Answer: Hamasien.

questions.prompt: In the Sahel the Bet Asghede gave rise to the
options: Habab, Ad Tekles and Ad Temariam
questions.explanation:
Textbook: 'In Sahel the Bet Asghede gave rise to the Habab, Ad Tekles, and Ad Temariam.'
Answer: Habab, Ad Tekles and Ad Temariam.

questions.prompt: The Ottoman Turks occupied Massawa and Hirghigo in
questions.explanation:
Textbook: 'the Ottoman Turks occupied Massawa and Hirghigo in 1557.'
Answer: 1557.

questions.prompt: The major gateway for the coming of Islam to Eritrea was the
questions.explanation:
Textbook: 'The Dahlak islands were the major gateway for the coming of Islam to our country.'
Answer: Dahlak islands.

questions.prompt: Which Eritrean language belongs to the Semitic group?
questions.explanation:
Tigrinya, Tigre and Arabic (Rashaida) are Semitic.
Answer: Tigrinya.
